question: Endometriosis is a benign inflammatory disease that consists of the appearance and growth of endometrium-like tissue outside of the uterus, which can cause chronic pelvic pain, infertility and various urinary tract disorders. It affects around 10 % of women of reproductive age and is usually found in the pelvis, intestine, diaphragm and pleural cavity.

This disease has a serious impact on patients’ quality of life and affects both their working lives and their mental health, with stress, anxiety and depression being some of the main consequences. Although endometriosis is widespread, there is no cure and diagnosis tends to take several years, largely due to the complexity of its symptoms and the lack of specific markers. Considering the above: 1.
What measures does the Commission intend to take to speed up and improve the diagnosis and early detection of endometriosis?
Is the Commission considering funding research into the causes of endometriosis and its therapeutic solutions?
What projects or treatments is the Commission currently supporting?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.2.2026) Member States are responsible for organisation and delivery of medical care1, including detection, diagnosis and treatment of diseases.

The Commission supports Member States in reducing the burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs)2, including conditions such as endometriosis, through the ‘Healthier Together’ EU NCD initiative3 with the financial support of the EU4Health programme4.

Together with the Expert Group on Public Health5, the Commission also supports the exchange of best practices among Member States via the EU Best Practice Portal on Public Health6. Over EUR 2 billion have been invested in research and innovation projects related to women’s health through the EU’s research and innovation framework programmes, Horizon 20207 and Horizon Europe8.

This includes 15 research projects on endometriosis worth EUR 47 million. The current R&I framework programme ‘Horizon Europe’ offers a variety of funding opportunities, including broadly defined calls under the ‘Health’ Cluster9. More information about opened and upcoming funding opportunities for research on gynaecological diseases, including endometriosis, can be found on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal10.

The EU is at the forefront of supporting research and innovation with the aim to improve and protect the health and well-being of citizens by developing innovative solutions to prevent, diagnose, treat and cure diseases. For instance, the project MultiMENDo11 looks for diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers, as well as new therapeutic approaches for endometriosis using menstrual fluid.
The projects EUmetriosis12 develops an integrated approach to enhance understanding, diagnosis, tailored management of endometriosis and empowerment of patients with this disease.
